# Shopware Storefront — CMS element, resolver and template map

Shopping Experiences render a page from sections, blocks and elements. An element is the smallest unit and the one that carries data: its resolver runs server-side and attaches the result, which the template reads as `element.data`.

**20 administration elements, 19 resolvers, 21 element templates; 39 administration blocks and 40 block templates.**

- [How a slot is rendered](#how-a-slot-is-rendered)

## The four parts of an element

One element type name ties four files together. The name is the join key everywhere: in `registerCmsElement({name})`, in the resolver's `getType()`, and in the template filename.

| Part | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Registration | `administration/.../sw-cms/elements/<name>/index.ts` | Declares the element and its `defaultConfig` — the fields the editor can set |
| Editor components | `component/`, `config/`, `preview/` beside it | How the element looks while editing, its settings form, its thumbnail |
| Resolver | `core/.../Cms/<Name>CmsElementResolver.php` | Loads data server-side; `getType()` returns the same name |
| Storefront template | `storefront/element/cms-element-<name>.html.twig` | Renders it, reading `element.config` and `element.data` |

A field in `defaultConfig` becomes `element.config.<field>.value` in Twig. That is the contract between the two ends: adding a configuration field means adding it to `defaultConfig` and reading it in the template.

## How a slot is rendered

```
cms_page -> section -> block -> slot
  slot.type            e.g. 'product-slider'
  -> resolver          getType() returns the same string
       collect()       declares the criteria, batched across all slots
       enrich()        calls $slot->setData(...)
  -> cms-element-<type>.html.twig
       element.data    what enrich() attached
       element.config  what the editor configured in the administration
```

`collect()` returning `null` means nothing is loaded for that slot. Configuration is read through `element.config.<field>.value` in Twig, and through `$slot->getFieldConfig()` in PHP.

## Element configuration fields

What the editor can configure per element, and therefore what the template can read as `element.config.<field>.value`.

Each field is an object, never a bare value. In PHP reach it through `$slot->getFieldConfig()->get('<field>')`, which returns a `FieldConfig` carrying `getSource()`, `getValue()`, plus typed accessors such as `getStringValue()` and `getArrayValue()`.

**The four sources** a field can carry, from `FieldConfig`:

- **`static`** — the editor typed a literal value. `getValue()` returns it directly. This is what every default below declares.
- **`mapped`** — the value is a path into the current entity, such as `product.name`. Resolve it against the `EntityResolverContext`; the raw value is the path, not the content.
- **`default`** — a placeholder the element falls back to, typically a demo image.
- **`product_stream`** — the value is a product stream id the resolver turns into a criteria filter.

A field with an `entity` declares that its value is an id of that entity. The resolver fetches it in `collect()` and attaches the loaded record in `enrich()`, so the template reads the object from `element.data`, not from `element.config`.

Elements with no configuration at all: `category-navigation`, `sidebar-filter`. They render from context alone and expose nothing to configure.

## Element templates without a resolver

These render without a server-side resolver. They read another slot's data, or fetch their own over a route at runtime.

- `storefront/element/cms-element-sidebar-filter.html.twig`
- `storefront/element/cms-element-wishlist-listing.html.twig`

## Blocks and the slots they declare

A block arranges elements and has no resolver of its own. Its registration names the slots it offers and the element type each slot takes by default, and its template includes `cms-element-<type>.html.twig` for each one.

| Block | Category | Slots (name: default type) | Template |
|---|---|---|---|
| `app-renderer` | — | — | `storefront/block/cms-block-app-renderer.html.twig` |
| `category-heading` | commerce | `content`: `category-name` | `storefront/block/cms-block-category-heading.html.twig` |
| `category-navigation` | sidebar | `content`: `category-navigation` | `storefront/block/cms-block-category-navigation.html.twig` |
| `center-text` | text-image | `left`: `image`, `center`: `text`, `right`: `image` | `storefront/block/cms-block-center-text.html.twig` |
| `cross-selling` | commerce | `content`: `cross-selling` | `storefront/block/cms-block-cross-selling.html.twig` |
| `form` | form | `content`: `form` | `storefront/block/cms-block-form.html.twig` |
| `gallery-buybox` | commerce | `left`: `image-gallery`, `right`: `buy-box` | `storefront/block/cms-block-gallery-buybox.html.twig` |
